transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-25
Start time: 11:00am PT / 19:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Rivera (Redwood SE), Dr. Aisha Kaur (LumenPath CISO), Miguel Ortega (Head of MLOps), Sandra Lee (Privacy Counsel), Noah Patel (Platform)

---
Summary (auto):
High-level compliance review: confirm no-training-on-customer-data commitments, prompt ephemerality (how long prompts are retained), KMS/encryption approach, RBAC/SSO integration, audit log fidelity, and EU data residency options. Customer has PHI concerns for a pilot with clinical notes. Redwood AE/SE to share SOC2/ISO docs + KMS architecture.

Topics: SOC 2, ISO, RBAC/SSO, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM, encryption-at-rest, prompt retention, PII/PHI handling, no-train confirmation, audit logs, data residency (EU), pilot benchmarks

---
00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): hey everyone thanks for joining on time, um we want to be mindful of schedules so quick intros then jump into the compliance asks.
00:12 Speaker 2 (Dr. Aisha Kaur): hi all, this is Aisha, im the CISO at LumenPath, joining with Miguel and Sandra. we're evaluating inference providers for a pilot with clinical transcription, so PHI is central.
00:22 Speaker 3 (Miguel): hey, Miguel here. main concerns are latency and how prompts are handled, we cannot have any training on customer data, and need clear residency for EU patients.
00:30 Speaker 1 (Maya): absolutely. Ethan from our SE team will walk through the tech controls then we can go into the legal/compliance items. Ethan?
00:38 Speaker 4 (Ethan): thanks. quick note: apologies if audio is rough i m on a train, bear with me. i'll run through our architectural controls: encryption, KMS options, and retention.
00:50 Speaker 4 (Ethan): first, on 'no training' -- Redwood has a contractual no-train promise for customer data on our hosted offering; that is, we do not use customer prompts/outputs to update model weights. the platform also supports an explicit flag per-tenant to disable any usage for feature improvements.
01:12 Speaker 2 (Dr. Aisha Kaur): can you clarify that is that a legal pledge or technical enforcement? we need something enforceable and auditable.
01:20 Speaker 4 (Ethan): good question. it's both: contractually it's in our DPA and terms; technically we have a tenant isolation layer that prevents data from the customer from being queued into model training pipelines. it's a separation of our metrics/telemetry streams. caveat: absolutely want to show you the controls and audit logs that prove that pipeline is separate.
01:36 Speaker 3 (Miguel): okay, audit logs are key. what do your logs capture? request/response? prompt hashes? IP?
01:44 Speaker 4 (Ethan): we capture request metadata, timestamps, model variant used, latency and token counts. payloads are not routinely stored long-term in the hosted default; ephemeral caching is used for performance but with TTL configured per-customer. We can surface per-request audit trails to customers via the console or via S3 exports for Dedicated/Private.
02:05 Speaker 5 (Sandra Lee): when you say payloads are not stored long-term, what's the default TTL? and is there an option for immediate deletion after response?
02:13 Speaker 4 (Ethan): default for hosted trial customers is 30 days for logs (metrics), but prompt content is ephemeral at 24 hours by default; enterprise customers can set shorter TTLs, down to 0 (ephemeral/no retention) on Dedicated or Private deployments. Note: some edge caches may persist for short periods to support streaming completion—but we can configure that.
02:33 Speaker 2 (Dr. Aisha Kaur): PHI means we need guaranteed no retention unless we have explicit encryption controls and KMS. can you explain your KMS options?
02:41 Speaker 4 (Ethan): sure. we support customer-managed keys (CMK) via cloud KMS (AWS KMS / Azure KeyVault / GCP KMS) for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys by default, and CMK as an enterprise add-on. We also have an HSM-backed option for FIPS 140-2/3 compliance in our Private install.
03:02 Speaker 3 (Miguel): how are keys used? is payload encrypted at rest and in transit?
03:07 Speaker 4 (Ethan): in transit is TLS 1.2+; at rest everything is encrypted. If you use CMK, the DEK (data encryption key) is wrapped by the CMK—standard envelope encryption. For logs and S3 exports we can optionally encrypt with your key.
03:20 Speaker 5 (Sandra Lee): if we use CMK, can we revoke access and have Redwood lose access to unencrypted data? that's a critical legal ask for some of our partners.
03:29 Speaker 4 (Ethan): yes, key rotation and revocation are supported. revocation will prevent future decrypts, but note that if you revoke and you have snapshots that Redwood controls, we recommend an explicit data destruction workflow. We'll include the caveats in the architecture doc.
03:44 Speaker 1 (Maya): quick interject — we have a diagram and sample KMS policy Ethan will send, it's in the security packet.
03:52 Speaker 6 (Noah Patel): Noah here—on residency: we need to know what parts of the stack can be pinned to eu regions. can you confirm?
04:00 Speaker 4 (Ethan): we support region pinning for data and compute on Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we run region-specific clusters in eu-west and eu-north, and you can request that your tenant's traffic is routed to EU clusters with contractual SLA.
04:17 Speaker 2 (Dr. Aisha Kaur): good. is metadata (like logs and request ids) also kept in EU when region pinned?
04:24 Speaker 4 (Ethan): yes, everything tied to the tenant can be set to EU-only. we will need to provision a tenant in the EU region which includes storing logs, audit trails, and backups in EU zones.
04:36 Speaker 3 (Miguel): RBAC and SSO—we use Okta, want SCIM provisioning, SAML SSO, and fine-grained RBAC for access to logs and model controls.
04:47 Speaker 4 (Ethan): we support SAML SSO and SCIM user provisioning; RBAC includes roles for billing, admin, developer, and read-only auditor. Custom roles are available on Dedicated/Private. We also have an audit log for admin actions (role changes, key rotations, model rollouts).
05:05 Speaker 5 (Sandra Lee): is the admin audit log tamper-evident? we need chain-of-custody assurance for future audits.
05:12 Speaker 4 (Ethan): logs are write-once and append-only in our internal system with integrity hashes, and we can ship an immutable export to your S3 with object lock enabled. again, Dedicated/Private gives the most assurances around chain-of-custody.
05:28 Speaker 2 (Dr. Aisha Kaur): okay, what about model fallbacks—if a model is deprecated or an edge fallback triggers, do you route to different models that might have different training policies? i.e., could a fallback inadvertently use a model trained on public data that is allowed to be finetuned on aggregated customer data?
05:48 Speaker 4 (Ethan): good catch. our fallback policy routes requests to compatible model variants vetted by our compliance team. None of the fallback variants are trained on customer data. We maintain model lineage and can provide a compatibility matrix. There is a policy to never route EU-pinned tenants to models that are under experimental training.
06:06 Speaker 3 (Miguel): we need to block any analytics that could infer patient info from aggregated logs—are there redaction hooks or PII scrubbing pre-send?
06:16 Speaker 4 (Ethan): Redwood offers client-side redaction hooks in SDKs, and we provide server-side redaction modules for common PII/PHI patterns (names, MRN, SSN). We can also run a privacy-preserving hash or tokenization pre-ingest upon request. For the pilot we recommend client-side tokenization plus server-side validation.
06:33 Speaker 5 (Sandra Lee): what about consent and legal signage—if a user asks for data deletion, how quickly can you purge prompts?
06:40 Speaker 4 (Ethan): with enterprise controls we can support on-request deletion within 24 hours; for Dedicated/Private you can set policy to purge immediately. We'll document the deletion workflow in the DPA addendum.
06:52 Speaker 1 (Maya): quick note—we'll attach a sample DPA clause that includes no-training language and deletion SLA.
06:58 Speaker 2 (Dr. Aisha Kaur): can you show me an example audit export? we like csvS that have timestamps, user ids, action, request id but not full content.
07:07 Speaker 4 (Ethan): yes, we can produce redacted exports. format: timestamp, tenant id, user id, action, request id, model, latency, token_count. content/payload columns are omitted unless requested and then encrypted.
07:21 Speaker 3 (Miguel): who within Redwood has access to decrypted payloads for debugging? we need a list of roles and justifications.
07:29 Speaker 4 (Ethan): only a small security/infra ops team has on-call access to decrypted payloads for live debugging, and access is tightly controlled via RBAC with short-lived creds, and each access is logged. We'll provide a current list of on-call roles and typical justifications.
07:44 Speaker 5 (Sandra Lee): any third-party subprocessors that might see data?
07:48 Speaker 4 (Ethan): we use cloud providers for infra (AWS, GCP, Azure), and in Hosted we may use managed observability vendors; all subprocessors are disclosed in the DPA and covered under flow-downs. For Dedicated/Private, fewer subprocessors since you control more of the infra.
07:59 Speaker 2 (Dr. Aisha Kaur): licensing question: if we move to Dedicated and later to Private, does the no-training guarantee persist? and contractually is it the same?
08:10 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes, no-training is contractual across offerings. Implementation differs: Hosted uses tenant flags and org-level policies; Dedicated/Private provide more technical isolation. We'll capture these differences in the handoff doc.
08:20 Speaker 3 (Miguel): latency constraints—encryption with deep HSM calls sometimes increases latency, how do you mitigate?
08:28 Speaker 4 (Ethan): we do envelope encryption so HSM calls are for key unwrap only and cached DEKs lower latency. Also we offer edge caches for tokenization/kv cache that are encrypted in memory. For stricter compliance we can pre-warm keys and provision dedicated HSMs in the region.
08:46 Speaker 2 (Dr. Aisha Kaur): audit frequency—how often do you run internal compliance scans and pen-tests?
08:53 Speaker 4 (Ethan): annual third-party pen tests, quarterly internal vulnerability scans, and continuous threat monitoring. SOC 2 Type II audits are annual; ISO 27001 recertification cadence is annual. We'll include the latest reports.
09:06 Speaker 5 (Sandra Lee): do you support data residency by tenant group, e.g., some datasets EU-only, others global?
09:15 Speaker 4 (Ethan): yes, you can set residency per-tenant or per-route. For mixed workloads we recommend separate tenants to avoid cross-region leakage.
09:25 Speaker 3 (Miguel): what's the recommended pilot configuration for our clinical notes PHI workload? hosted or dedicated?
09:33 Speaker 1 (Maya): for a short pilot with minimal infra lift, Hosted with CMK + EU pinning and strict TTL (0-24h) and client-side tokenization could work. If you require absolute isolation or object-lock for forensic chain-of-custody, Dedicated would be the recommended next step.
09:49 Speaker 2 (Dr. Aisha Kaur): we prefer Dedicated for the pilot if the cost is reasonable. need a quote.
09:55 Speaker 1 (Maya): noted, i'll loop in GTM for a dedicated pilot quote.
10:00 Speaker 6 (Noah): minor thing: can we disable streaming cache to ensure chunks arent buffered for other tenants?
10:06 Speaker 4 (Ethan): yes, streaming buffer TTL can be set to 0 and isolated per-tenant on Dedicated/Private.
10:12 Speaker 5 (Sandra Lee): legal will need a redlined DPA; is there a template?
10:15 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes, we'll share a DPA template and the no-training addendum.
10:20 Speaker 2 (Dr. Aisha Kaur): last question — you said model lineage and compatibility matrix; can we get that to ensure none of the models used are under a training program that ingests customer prompts?
10:30 Speaker 4 (Ethan): yes, we'll share the matrix and highlight variants allowed for EU tenants and those excluded from training.
10:38 Speaker 1 (Maya): ok wrapping up — recap of next steps and action items. we'll send SOC2/ISO, KMS diagram, DPA sample, and schedule the pilot benchmark.
10:47 Speaker 2 (Dr. Aisha Kaur): thank you everyone. appreciate the transparency.
10:52 Speaker 1 (Maya): thanks all, we'll follow up by Friday.
